import asyncio
import pytest

import falcon
import falcon.util
from falcon.util.deprecation import DeprecatedWarning


async def _dummy_coro(delay: float = 0.0):
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
    return 'ok'


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_create_task_emits_deprecated_warning():
    with pytest.warns(DeprecatedWarning, match='falcon.util.create_task is deprecated'):
        task = falcon.util.create_task(_dummy_coro(0.001))
    assert isinstance(task, asyncio.Task)
    await task


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_get_running_loop_emits_deprecated_warning():
    with pytest.warns(
        DeprecatedWarning, match='falcon.util.get_running_loop is deprecated'
    ):
        loop = falcon.util.get_running_loop()
    assert isinstance(loop, asyncio.AbstractEventLoop)
    # Double-check the loop is the current one
    assert loop is asyncio.get_running_loop()


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_front_door_aliases_emit_deprecated_warning():
    # Ensure front-door exports (falcon.create_task, falcon.get_running_loop)
    # also emit deprecation warnings
    with pytest.warns(DeprecatedWarning, match='falcon.util.create_task is deprecated'):
        t = falcon.create_task(_dummy_coro(0.001))
    assert isinstance(t, asyncio.Task)
    await t

    with pytest.warns(
        DeprecatedWarning, match='falcon.util.get_running_loop is deprecated'
    ):
        lp = falcon.get_running_loop()
    assert lp is asyncio.get_running_loop()
